questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
choices: A patient trying to quit smoking by using a nicotine patch may experience osmotic diarrhea.
Curtailing oral intake in a patient with a VIPoma will help reduce the diarrhea.
Inflammatory diarrhea is characterized by mucosal damage.
Exceedingly rapid transit may be seen in motility diarrhea.

evidence.quote: Because VIPoma, in case of that, it's, it's by tumor. There is unregulated excessive um secretion of VIB and that leads to diarrhea. So you can't really, even if you curtail oral intake, that's not going to help us.

questions.note:
B is the incorrect statement. A VIPoma causes secretory diarrhea: VIP raises cAMP in crypt cells and drives chloride and water into the lumen whether or not the patient eats, so the diarrhea keeps going during fasting, with large volumes and night-time stools. The diarrhea that stops when the patient stops eating is osmotic diarrhea.
A is treated as true on this slide, but the lecture never covers nicotine. The osmotic causes it does list are poorly absorbed solutes such as lactose in lactase deficiency, sorbitol-sweetened gum and milk of magnesia, and a nicotine patch delivers no gut solute, so don't lean on this option.
C is true: inflammatory diarrhea from IBD or invasive or toxin-producing pathogens involves mucosal damage, with pain, fever and often blood.
D is true: motility diarrhea (for example, IBS or hyperthyroidism) moves contents through in minutes rather than hours.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
choices: Both norovirus and rotavirus lead to acute diarrhea, and a vaccine against rotavirus is available.
The life cycles of Giardia and E. histolytica consist of trophozoite and cyst forms, and these pathogens respond to antibiotics.
The toxins of V. cholerae, ETEC and S. aureus are all endotoxins.
SGLT-1 transports sodium and glucose, is tightly coupled with water movement, and is the basis for oral rehydration using glucose to enhance sodium absorption.

evidence.quote: This is incorrect, right? Why? Because these are all exotoxins.

questions.note:
C is the incorrect statement. Cholera toxin, the ETEC heat-labile and heat-stable toxins, and the staphylococcal enterotoxins are all exotoxins. They are proteins the bacteria secrete, and because they act on the gut lining they are called enterotoxins. Endotoxin is the lipopolysaccharide in the outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria, not a secreted protein.
A is true: norovirus and rotavirus are RNA viruses that cause acute diarrhea, and rotavirus vaccines have cut child mortality. Norovirus has no vaccine.
B is true: both protozoa cycle between trophozoites and cysts, and both are treated with metronidazole.
D is true: SGLT-1 moves sodium together with glucose and pulls water along, which is why oral rehydration solutions contain glucose.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
choices: Symptoms of nausea and violent vomiting due to Staphylococcus aureus develop slowly.
ETEC heat-labile toxin stimulates adenylate cyclase, increases cAMP and thus increases chloride secretion and water efflux.
ETEC heat-stable toxin stimulates guanylate cyclase, increases cGMP and thus decreases resorption of NaCl and H2O.
The pathophysiology of Clostridium difficile infection involves disruption of intercellular tight junctions.

evidence.quote: We do not agree with that, right? Because SRES has that pre-formed toxin, so it is really rapid. The symptoms do not develop very slowly.

questions.note:
A is the incorrect statement. S. aureus food poisoning comes on quickly, within a few hours. The enterotoxin is already formed in the food, so there is no incubation period while bacteria grow in the gut. It causes nausea and violent vomiting, with or without diarrhea.
B is true: heat-labile toxin activates adenylate cyclase, so cAMP rises and drives chloride secretion and water loss ("labile like the Air").
C is true: heat-stable toxin activates guanylate cyclase, so cGMP rises and NaCl and water absorption drops ("stable like the Ground").
D is true: C. difficile toxins A and B inactivate Rho family proteins, which collapses the cytoskeleton and opens the tight junctions between cells.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents to an urgent care center with nausea, vomiting and abdominal cramps. She felt well earlier in the day and played in a softball tournament, followed by a potluck lunch with the other players. Her symptoms began two hours after she got home. She denies fever and has had no diarrhea. Exam shows mild diffuse abdominal tenderness. Which of the following is responsible for this person's illness?
choices: Endotoxin
Bacterial invasion of the intestinal mucosa
Exotoxin formed prior to ingestion
Exotoxin formed after ingestion

evidence.quote: So, again, I just wanted to bring this that it was not chronic, only 2 hours. Endotoxin was not a good option. This was not a good option. So it was exotoxin uh prior to injection.
This is really important that these exotoxins are formed prior to the ingestion. So these are pre-formed toxins.

questions.note:
Exotoxin formed prior to ingestion. Vomiting within hours of a potluck meal, with no fever, is S. aureus food poisoning. The bacteria grow in food left out at warm temperatures and release enterotoxin there, and the toxin survives heat and stomach acid, so symptoms start fast. The toxin acts on the vagus nerve to trigger vomiting.
Endotoxin is gram-negative LPS. It drives fever and sepsis, not this quick afebrile vomiting illness.
Mucosal invasion causes inflammatory diarrhea with fever and often blood, which she doesn't have.
An exotoxin made after ingestion (as with ETEC or cholera) needs the bacteria to colonize first, so the illness starts later and is mostly watery diarrhea rather than vomiting.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman comes to the urgent care clinic with sudden onset of severe vomiting. She was at a picnic with her boyfriend a few hours earlier, eating barbecue, potato salad and cake. Shortly afterward she began vomiting and has vomited 5 times in the last 3 hours. She has no prior history of these symptoms. After a few hours of observation her symptoms resolve, and she is safely discharged home. Which of the following is the most likely cause of her vomiting?
choices: Viral infection
Hepatitis
Gallstones
Toxin ingestion from a spore-forming organism
Toxin ingestion from a non-spore-forming organism

evidence.quote: But they have given you potato salad, meaning it was not cooked, so then I would go with SRES that it was because it doesn't, it's not really heat resistant in that way where bacillus would be.

questions.note:
Toxin ingestion from a non-spore-forming organism. Picnic food like potato salad, sudden vomiting within hours, and recovery the same day is classic S. aureus food poisoning. S. aureus is a gram-positive coccus that does not form spores. It makes a heat-stable enterotoxin in the food before anyone eats it.
A viral infection such as norovirus has a longer incubation (about 12-24 hours) and lasts up to a few days, not a few hours.
Hepatitis would bring jaundice and liver symptoms over days, not brief vomiting after a meal.
Gallstones cause right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals. They don't cause a single self-limited bout of vomiting that clears within hours.
A spore-forming organism such as Bacillus cereus can also cause rapid vomiting, but its classic source is reheated rice. Potato salad and the S. aureus story in this lecture point to the non-spore-former.

*About the quote above*: "SRES" is speech-to-text for *S. aureus*. "Not really heat resistant" refers to the bacterium itself, which forms no spores, unlike *Bacillus*. Its preformed enterotoxin **is** heat-stable, which is why reheating the food does not prevent this illness.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is hospitalized with symptoms of necrotizing enterocolitis, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and fever. Radiologic findings show bowel wall thickening. Staphylococcal infection is suspected. Which one of the following explains the underlying mechanism of pathogenesis of the staphylococcal exotoxin?
choices: Activation of enterocyte cyclic GMP
Inactivation of regulatory pathways mediated by Rho family proteins
Activation of Gs-alpha through an ADP-ribosylation reaction
Stimulation of the vagus nerve in the abdominal viscera

evidence.quote: D, right? The stimulation of the vagus nerve in the abdominal viscera, that's the mechanism.

questions.note:
Stimulation of the vagus nerve in the abdominal viscera. Staphylococcal enterotoxins trigger vagal afferents in the gut, which signal the vomiting center in the brain. They also get through the gut lining and set off local immune activation and inflammatory mediators (histamine, leukotrienes, substance P), which can injure the stomach and upper small bowel.
Raising enterocyte cGMP is how the ETEC heat-stable toxin works.
Inactivating Rho family proteins is how C. difficile toxins A and B work.
ADP-ribosylation of Gs-alpha, which keeps adenylate cyclase switched on, is how cholera toxin and the ETEC heat-labile toxin work.
